title: Multilingual Transformer Fine-Tuning for Low-Resource Translation
summary: Fine-tuning Facebook AI's mBART on low-resource language pairs with efficient training tricks.

details.problem: Low-resource languages suffer from poor machine-translation quality because large pretrained models are optimized for high-resource pairs.
details.approach: Fine-tuned the pretrained Facebook AI Research mBART multilingual encoder-decoder model on low-resource language datasets to improve translation quality. Designed a complete NLP training pipeline including dataset preprocessing, tokenization, batching, and GPU-based training.
details.implementation: Used gradient accumulation and optimized batching to reduce memory usage during transformer training. Experimented with beam search and top-k sampling decoding strategies to analyse the effect on quality and inference speed.
details.results: Running controlled experiments comparing baseline pretrained performance with fine-tuned models across multiple language pairs. [ADD: specific metric improvements once experiments conclude.]
details.future: Add adapter-based fine-tuning (LoRA) and expand to additional language pairs.

title: NLP for Mental Health Diagnosis
summary: Classification system to detect mental health conditions from textual data using classical ML + NLP preprocessing.

details.problem: Early signals of mental-health difficulties often appear in written language. Automated screening could support — not replace — human care.
details.approach: Built preprocessing pipelines with NLTK and spaCy including tokenization, stop-word removal, and vectorization. Trained and evaluated multiple classical models (Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Logistic Regression).
details.implementation: Compared models across common text-classification metrics; visualised results with ROC curves, learning curves, and precision-recall analysis to understand model behaviour.
details.results: Comparative evaluation across models complete; findings are documented in the repo README.
details.future: Explore transformer-based baselines (DistilBERT) and multi-label formulations.

title: Chronicler — Timetable & Schedule System for SICSR
summary: Modern timetable experience for SICSR students built on MRBS, with a cleaner UI and faster filtering.

details.problem: The existing SICSR timetable interface was clunky; filtering was slow and the experience discouraged use.
details.approach: Rebuilt the student-facing timetable using MRBS as the backing engine with a thin, modern layer on top.
details.implementation: Key features: web scraper, data caching + validation, both web and textual UIs, CI/CD, and test coverage. Core philosophy: minimalistic, responsive, performant components.
details.results: Students can now access, filter, and read timetables in a far more intuitive flow.
details.future: Push notifications for schedule changes, calendar sync.

title: Network Intrusion Detection on UNSW-NB15
summary: ML + ANN pipeline detecting and classifying multiple network intrusions, with full comparative evaluation.

details.problem: Detect and classify multiple network intrusions using a real-time dataset.
details.approach: Preprocessed and balanced the UNSW-NB15 dataset; implemented Artificial Neural Networks and Random Forest classifiers.
details.implementation: Evaluated models with accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC analysis; co-authored a research manuscript (currently under peer review).
details.results: Manuscript submitted to a Scopus-indexed Q2 journal; under review.
details.future: Extend to ensemble models and streaming / online classification.
